# cleura_gardener_bootstrap (Resource)

Prepares an **OpenStack project for Gardener**. A project must be bootstrapped before any
`cleura_gardener_shoot` can be created in it: the bootstrap provisions the supporting
resources Gardener needs inside the project.

Projects created through the Cleura Cloud control panel are normally bootstrapped for you.
A project created with `cleura_openstack_project` is **not** — bootstrap it with this
resource before pointing a shoot at it.

!> **Warning: bootstrapping is irreversible.** The API offers only `POST .../bootstrap`.
There is **no endpoint to undo a bootstrap** and **none to read whether a project is
bootstrapped**. The provider warns at plan time before creating one. `terraform destroy`
removes the resource from state and warns you — the project stays bootstrapped in Cleura.

~> **This resource cannot detect drift.** Because nothing can be read back, `terraform plan`
never reports a difference for an existing bootstrap. Terraform trusts what is in state.

## Choosing the project

`project_id` defaults to the provider's `project_id`, which is the right choice when the
project already exists and the rest of your configuration targets it:

```terraform
resource "cleura_gardener_bootstrap" "default" {}
```

Set `project_id` explicitly to bootstrap a project **created in the same configuration**.
Provider configuration must be resolvable before the run starts, so the provider's
`project_id` can never refer to a `cleura_openstack_project` this provider manages — that is
a dependency cycle. Passing the ID to this resource avoids it.

### Deploying a shoot into a newly created project

`cleura_gardener_shoot` still takes its project from the **provider** configuration, so a
brand-new project reaches a shoot in **two applies**:

1. **First apply** — create the project, its users, and the bootstrap. Output the project ID.
2. **Second apply** — set the provider's `project_id` (or `CLEURA_PROJECT_ID`) to that value
   and add the `cleura_gardener_shoot`.

Splitting the two into separate root modules or workspaces makes the boundary explicit and
keeps the shoot's provider configuration a plain literal or variable.

### Prerequisites

The provider must be authenticated and have a `cloud` and `region`; both are recorded on the
resource. `project_id` is required, from either this resource or the provider. See the
provider's [Authentication](../index.md#authentication) documentation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Prepare a project for Gardener. A project must be bootstrapped before any
# cleura_gardener_shoot can be created in it.

# The common case: bootstrap the project the provider is already pointed at.
resource "cleura_gardener_bootstrap" "default" {}

# Bootstrapping a project created in the same configuration. The provider's
# project_id has to be known before the run starts, so it cannot refer to a
# project this provider creates; pass the ID to the resource instead.
resource "cleura_openstack_project" "team" {
  name        = "team-sandbox"
  description = "Sandbox for the platform team"
}

resource "cleura_gardener_bootstrap" "team" {
  project_id = cleura_openstack_project.team.id
}

output "bootstrapped_project_id" {
  value = cleura_gardener_bootstrap.team.project_id
}
```

## Import

Importing records that a project is bootstrapped. Nothing is verified, because the API
offers no way to ask — importing a project that was never bootstrapped will make Terraform
believe it was.

```shell
# Adopt a project that is already bootstrapped (for example one created through
# the Cleura Cloud control panel). The import ID is the OpenStack project ID.
terraform import cleura_gardener_bootstrap.default 5bc1a0e0a2fa4a6b9f4b8f0f2ba7b1cd
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `project_id` (String) OpenStack project to bootstrap. Defaults to the provider's `project_id`. Set it explicitly to bootstrap a project created in the same configuration — the provider's `project_id` must be known before the run starts, so it cannot refer to a `cleura_openstack_project` managed by this provider. Changing it forces replacement (a bootstrap of the new project).

### Read-Only

- `cloud` (String) Cleura cloud the project was bootstrapped in, taken from the provider configuration.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the bootstrap, in the form `<cloud>/<region>/<project_id>`.
- `region` (String) OpenStack region the project was bootstrapped in, taken from the provider configuration.
